Let $(V,\eta)$ be a Lorentz vector space of signature $(-,+,+,+)$
([[def-lorentz-form-and-inertia]]), with associated quadratic form
$q(v)=\eta(v,v)$. A vector $v\in V$ is

- **timelike** when $q(v)<0$;
- **null**, or **lightlike**, when $v\neq 0$ and $q(v)=0$;
- **spacelike** when $q(v)>0$;
- **causal** when it is timelike or null.

The zero vector $0\in V$ satisfies $q(0)=0$ and is consequently **none** of
timelike, null or spacelike: the null case explicitly excludes it, and the
timelike and spacelike cases exclude it by $q(0)=0$ together with the strict
inequalities. The **causal character** of a nonzero vector $v$ is the sign of
the real number $q(v)$, and the three names are attached to the three signs as
above. When no confusion arises, the pairing $\eta$ itself is written
$\langle v,w\rangle:=\eta(v,w)$.

**Each nonzero vector has exactly one causal character.** For a nonzero
$v\in V$ the real number $q(v)$ satisfies exactly one of $q(v)<0$, $q(v)=0$,
$q(v)>0$ by trichotomy of the order on $\mathbb R$, so $v$ is timelike, null or
spacelike, and no two of the three alternatives can hold at once. The causal
vectors are therefore exactly the nonzero vectors that are timelike or null,
and the zero vector is causal in no sense introduced here.

Use the SI quantities, coordinate convention, and primitive/derived distinction of [[def-emg-geometry-units]], and the zero-cosmological-constant geometric electrovac flux normalization of [[def-emg-xs-geometric-electrovac]]. This definition is the model-local parameter map for the RN and KN ansatz families; it is not a claim that nature contains an object with these parameters.

Take $G_N>0$, $c>0$, and $\mu_0>0$ as the gravitational and electromagnetic constants used by this coupled model, with $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$. Let $m_*>0$ be a selected SI mass parameter in kg, $J\in\mathbb R$ a selected angular-momentum parameter in kg m$^2$ s$^{-1}$, $Q_e\in\mathbb R$ a selected electric charge parameter in C, and $\Phi_B\in\mathbb R$ a selected magnetic flux in Wb through an oriented sphere. These are the chosen SI inputs of this parametrization; this role is local to the solution families and is not a universal ontology for mass, angular momentum, or charge.

For the geometric flux integrals below, retain the $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ convention explicitly stated by [[def-emg-xs-geometric-electrovac]] and defined by [[def-countable-choice]]. No arbitrary-index choice principle or magnetic-charge quantization is added.

Set

$$\alpha:=\sqrt{\frac{4\pi G_N}{\mu_0c^4}},\qquad \mathcal F:=\alpha F,$$

where $F$ is the SI electromagnetic two-form of [[def-emg-geometry-units]] and $\mathcal F$ is its geometric normalization. In length coordinates $F_{ab}$ has unit T, $\mathcal F_{ab}$ has unit m$^{-1}$, and $\alpha$ has unit T$^{-1}$m$^{-1}$. For an oriented sphere $S$, write the geometric flux parameters as

$$q_e:=\frac{1}{4\pi}\int_S\star_g\mathcal F,\qquad q_m:=\frac{1}{4\pi}\int_S\mathcal F.$$

The SI electric-flux convention is $Q_e=\varepsilon_0c\int_S\star_gF$, and the magnetic quantity used here is the flux $\Phi_B=\int_S F$. Thus

$$q_e=\frac{\alpha}{4\pi\varepsilon_0c}Q_e=\sqrt{\frac{G_N}{4\pi\varepsilon_0c^4}}\,Q_e,\qquad q_m=\frac{\alpha}{4\pi}\Phi_B.$$

The second equality in the electric formula uses the exact SI relation $\varepsilon_0\mu_0c^2=1$. Both $q_e$ and $q_m$ have units of length; $q_m$ is a flux parameter and is not assigned a universal SI magnetic-charge convention. If one separately chooses the convention $Q_m:=\Phi_B/\mu_0$ with unit A m, then the same definition reads $q_m=\sqrt{G_N\mu_0/(4\pi c^4)}\,Q_m$; this optional relabeling adds no new physical assumption or quantization rule.

For the metric parameters, set

$$M:=\frac{G_Nm_*}{c^2},\qquad a:=\frac{J}{m_*c},\qquad Q_{\mathrm{geom}}^2:=q_e^2+q_m^2.$$

Here $M$, $a$, $q_e$, and $q_m$ are derived length parameters, while $m_*$, $J$, $Q_e$, $\Phi_B$, $G_N$, $c$, and $\mu_0$ are the selected inputs of this map. The dimensionless metric coefficients use $M/r$, $a/r$, and $Q_{\mathrm{geom}}^2/r^2$. Horizon radii, areas, angular velocities, and surface gravities are further derived quantities of a specified solution, not additional primitive inputs.

These parameter identifications do not establish that $M$ equals an ADM or Komar mass, or that $J$ equals an ADM or Komar angular momentum; such identifications need their own global hypotheses and proofs. They supply no empirical values for $G_N$ or $\mu_0$, no measured black-hole parameters, no global potential in a nonzero magnetic-flux sector, and no claim of charge quantization. The source treatments use differing signatures, charge normalizations, and natural or Gaussian unit conventions; the SI formulas above are fixed by the stated local conventions and are not copied without conversion.

Use the smooth covariant metric and signature conventions of [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]] and the smooth real form spaces $\Omega^k(U)$ of [[def-smooth-differential-k-form]]. Geometric electric flux-length normalization means the convention in [[def-emg-xs-geometric-electrovac]]; its field equations are not hypotheses in this coordinate definition.

Let $M,a,q\in\mathbb R$ have units of metres. Write
$$\Sigma(r,\theta):=r^2+a^2\cos^2\theta,\quad \Delta(r):=r^2-2Mr+a^2+q^2,\quad R(r):=r^2+a^2,\quad B(\theta):=\sin^2\theta.$$
Let $U$ be an open subset of the Boyer-Lindquist coordinate region
$\{(x^0,r,\theta,\phi):\Sigma>0,\ \Delta\ne0,\ 0<\theta<\pi\}$.
Coordinates $x^0,r$ have units of metres and $\theta,\phi$ are dimensionless.
On $U$ define
$$g=-\frac{\Delta}{\Sigma}(dx^0-aB\,d\phi)^2 +\frac{\Sigma}{\Delta}\,dr^2+\Sigma\,d\theta^2 +\frac{B}{\Sigma}(R\,d\phi-a\,dx^0)^2,\qquad \mathcal A=-\frac{qr}{\Sigma}(dx^0-aB\,d\phi),\quad\mathcal F:=d\mathcal A.$$
The metric is the exact real symmetric tensor given by this display; no value
on $\Delta=0$, the axes $\theta=0,\pi$, or $\Sigma=0$ is part of this
definition. The scalar $q$ is a geometric electric flux-length parameter; no
SI conversion is fixed in this Definition.

**Well-definedness on the stated patch.** In the coordinates
$(x^0,r,y,\phi)$ with $y=\cos\theta$ and $b=1-y^2$, the coordinate change is
a smooth diffeomorphism because $dy/d\theta=-\sin\theta\ne0$. The metric
matrix has
$$g_{00}=-\frac{\Delta-a^2b}{\Sigma},\quad g_{03}=-\frac{ab(R-\Delta)}{\Sigma},\quad g_{33}=\frac{b(R^2-a^2\Delta b)}{\Sigma},\quad g_{11}=\frac{\Sigma}{\Delta},\quad g_{22}=\frac{\Sigma}{b}.$$
The inverse has nonzero entries
$$g^{00}=-\frac{R^2-a^2\Delta b}{\Sigma\Delta},\quad g^{03}=-\frac{a(R-\Delta)}{\Sigma\Delta},\quad g^{33}=\frac{\Delta-a^2b}{\Sigma\Delta b},\quad g^{11}=\frac{\Delta}{\Sigma},\quad g^{22}=\frac{b}{\Sigma}.$$
Multiplying the $0,3$ blocks and the reciprocal $1,1$ and $2,2$ entries
gives $gg^{-1}=I_4$.
The $t,\phi$ block determinant is $-\Delta b$, and the full determinant is
$-\Sigma^2$ in these coordinates. If $\Delta>0$, the $t,\phi$ block has one
positive and one negative eigenvalue while the $r,\theta$ entries are positive.
If $\Delta<0$, $g_{33}>0$ and the $t,\phi$ block has positive determinant,
hence is positive definite, while $g_{11}<0$ and $g_{22}>0$. Thus $g$ is
nondegenerate of signature $(-,+,+,+)$ on every component of $U$. Since this
is a coordinate patch, a smooth time orientation may be supplied locally;
the coordinate tensors and their closedness do not depend on that choice.

The potential is a smooth real one-form on $U$ because $\Sigma>0$, so $\mathcal F$
is a smooth real two-form. The coordinate formula in [[thm-local-coordinate-formula-for-the-exterior-derivative]] defines $\mathcal F=d\mathcal A$ componentwise. Applying it again pairs each second partial of a potential coefficient with its reversed-order partial and opposite wedge sign. They cancel by [[thm-clairaut-schwarz-mixed-partials]], since every coefficient is smooth; hence $d\mathcal F=d^2\mathcal A=0$. This definition is
only on the pole-free Boyer-Lindquist patch and asserts no global potential,
axis extension, horizon extension, or global topology.

Let $M,a,q\in\mathbb R$ have units of metres, choose $R_0>4|M|$, and
set
$$\mathcal X:=\mathbb R_{x^0}\times(R_0,\infty)_r\times S^2,\qquad R=r^2+a^2,\quad b=1-Z^2,\quad \Sigma=r^2+a^2Z^2,\quad \Delta=r^2-2Mr+a^2+q^2,$$
where $S^2=\{(X,Y,Z)\in\mathbb R^3:X^2+Y^2+Z^2=1\}$ has its induced
unit round metric $\gamma$ and outward area form $\omega$.
Specify the sphere smooth structure by [[def-gr-schwarzschild-exterior-model]],
Definition (b): on $S^2\setminus\{(0,0,\varepsilon)\}$ use
$\sigma_\varepsilon(X,Y,Z)=(X,Y)/(1-\varepsilon Z)$, $\varepsilon=\pm1$.
With $h=u_1^2+u_2^2$, the inverse is
$u\mapsto(2u_1,2u_2,\varepsilon(h-1))/(1+h)$, and the transition
on $h>0$ is $u\mapsto u/h$. These maps are smooth on their domains.
Give $\mathcal X$ the maximal atlas generated by the product charts
$(x^0,r,p)\mapsto(x^0,r,\sigma_\varepsilon(p))$;
its transitions leave $x^0,r$ fixed and apply the displayed sphere transition.
The product is Hausdorff and second countable as a subspace of $\mathbb R^5$,
using rational balls for a countable basis. The inverse parametrizations
make the sphere inclusion smooth with injective differential, so
$\gamma_p(u,v)=u\cdot v$ and $\omega_p(u,v)=\det(p,u,v)$
are smooth tensors with the stated outward orientation. Write
$$\lambda:=X\,dY-Y\,dX,\qquad \bar g:=-\frac{\Delta-a^2b}{\Sigma}(dx^0)^2 +\frac{\Sigma}{\Delta}\,dr^2+\Sigma\gamma +\frac{a^2(R+\Sigma-\Delta)}{\Sigma}\lambda^2 -\frac{2a(R-\Delta)}{\Sigma}\,dx^0\odot\lambda,$$
$$\bar{\mathcal A}:=-\frac{qr}{\Sigma}(dx^0-a\lambda),\qquad \bar{\mathcal F}:=d\bar{\mathcal A}.$$
Here $\lambda^2=\lambda\otimes\lambda$ and
$u\odot v=(u\otimes v+v\otimes u)/2$. This is the **full-sphere exterior
extension** of the pole-free datum in [[def-emg-xs-kn-data]]. The coordinates
$x^0,r$ and parameters $M,a,q$ have units of metres; sphere coordinates
are dimensionless. The field $\bar{\mathcal F}$ is the geometric
length-normalized two-form and no SI conversion is part of this definition.

Let $M$ be the smooth, boundaryless, oriented and time-oriented Lorentzian
four-manifold of [[def-emg-geometry-units]], with metric $g$ of signature
$(-,+,+,+)$ and the curvature convention of
[[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. Let $U\subseteq M$ be open. Take a smooth real
two-form $F$ on $U$. For each application, fix one explicitly named smooth
classical matter-model instance
$$\mathcal M=(\mathcal C_m,\mathcal E_m,\mathsf J_m,\mathsf T_m).$$
For each admitted pair $(g,F)$, $\mathcal C_m[g,F]$ is a specified set of
smooth matter-field configurations on $U$, including their field bundles and
regularity; $\mathcal E_m[g,F;\Psi]$ is the explicit system of equations and
constraints that defines the admissible configurations; and
$\mathsf J_m[g,F;\Psi]$ and $\mathsf T_m[g,F;\Psi]$ are specified maps from
those configurations to, respectively, smooth vector fields and smooth
symmetric covariant two-tensors on $U$. For an admissible configuration
$\Psi\in\mathcal C_m[g,F]$, set $j:=\mathsf J_m[g,F;\Psi]$ and
$T^m:=\mathsf T_m[g,F;\Psi]$. A consuming item must name the selected model and
state the exact field variables, equations, constraints, regularity, and
additional domain or initial-data hypotheses it uses. Those matter equations
and constraints are premises of that model instance; they are not supplied or
proved by this postulate. In particular, arbitrary independent smooth $j$ and
$T^m$ are not a matter-model instance merely because their types match.

There is also a named zero-matter instance $\mathcal M_0$: its configuration
set is the singleton $\{*\}$, it has no matter-field variables or additional
constraints, and $\mathsf J_0(*)=0$, $\mathsf T_0(*)=0$. Whenever a use sets
$j=0$ and $T^m=0$ without additional matter fields, it is this source-free
instance.

For an admissible $\Psi$, adopt $dF=0$ and
$\nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0j^b$ under the adopted convention of
[[post-emg-covariant-maxwell]]. This equation-based postulate then adds the
gravitational field law below, independently of any matter action.

Define the Einstein tensor by $G_{ab}:=\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}
-\tfrac12 Rg_{ab}$, using the curvature contractions of
[[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]], and define the smooth-field electromagnetic
stress tensor by

$$T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}:=\frac1{\mu_0}\left(F_{ac}F_b{}^c-\frac14g_{ab}F_{cd}F^{cd}\right).$$

For constant cosmological parameter $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$ and
$\kappa_E:=8\pi G_N/c^4$, adopt the additional equation-based gravitational
field law

$$G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa_E\left(T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}+T^m_{ab}\right).$$

Here $c>0$, $G_N>0$, and $\mu_0>0$ have the SI roles and units fixed in
[[def-emg-geometry-units]]; in length coordinates, $G_{ab}$ and
$\Lambda g_{ab}$ have units $\mathrm{m^{-2}}$, $T^{\mathrm{EM}}$ and $T^m$
have units $\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$, and $\kappa_E$ has units
$\mathrm{m\,J^{-1}}$. The source-free and sourced Maxwell equations remain
smooth-field postulates: point or sheet sources, distribution-valued products,
material excitation laws, and a global potential are outside this scope.

This is an equation-based adoption. It does not assume or imply the existence
of a matter action and is not derived from an action principle. The sources give
formulations in their own conventions; they motivate comparison but do not
establish a physical law or a solution-existence theorem.

For $M,a,q\in\mathbb R$, on every pole-free Boyer-Lindquist domain with

[[def-emg-xs-kn-data]] satisfy the equations below. In addition, for every
$R_0>4|M|$, the full-sphere exterior extension of
[[def-emg-xs-kn-full-sphere-exterior]] satisfies the same equations on

$$d\mathcal F=0,\qquad d(\star_g\mathcal F)=0,\qquad \operatorname{Ric}_{ij}=2\left(\mathcal F_{ik}\mathcal F_j{}^k -\frac14g_{ij}\mathcal F_{kl}\mathcal F^{kl}\right).$$

For arbitrary formal $c,\mu_0,G_N>0$, set $\alpha=\sqrt{4\pi G_N/(\mu_0c^4)}$, $F=\mathcal F/\alpha$, and $T_{ab}:=\mu_0^{-1}Q_g(F)_{ab}$. Then the same datum satisfies

$$dF=d(\star_gF)=0,\qquad S=0,\qquad G_{ab}=\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}=\frac{8\pi G_N}{c^4}T_{ab},$$

where $S$ is scalar curvature and $G_{ab}=\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}-\frac12Sg_{ab}$. This is the formal SI-to-geometric tensor normalization of [[lem-emg-maxwell-observer-stress]](d). It asserts neither measured parameter values nor a bundle realization for arbitrary flux. Let $(M,g,N,o)$ be the smooth, boundaryless, oriented and time-oriented
Lorentzian four-manifold of [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]], with signature
$(-,+,+,+)$, metric-selected connection $\nabla$ and oriented metric volume
form $\mathrm{vol}_g$. Let $F\in\Omega^2(M)$ be a smooth real two-form and
$j\in\Gamma(TM)$ a smooth vector field. Fix constants $\mu_0>0$ and $c>0$;
$\mu_0$ is a real coefficient here, and $c$ is the positive coordinate
conversion in $x^0=ct$ of [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. Assume the mathematical
field equations

$$dF=0,\qquad \nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0j^b.$$

The equations are conditional hypotheses, not physical postulates in this
mathematical item. Define $v\in\Gamma(TM)$ by $v^b:=\nabla_aF^{ab}$ and
define the current three-form by $\iota_j\mathrm{vol}_g$, the contraction
specified in [[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]]. Then:

**(a) Sign identity.** On $M$,

$$d(\star_gF)=-\iota_v\mathrm{vol}_g.$$

Consequently the sourced equation is equivalently

$$\nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0j^b\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad d(\star_gF)=\mu_0\iota_j\mathrm{vol}_g.$$

**(b) Current conservation.** Either equivalent sourced equation implies
$\nabla_aj^a=0$. This conclusion requires the sourced equation and $\mu_0>0$;
it does not require $dF=0$.

**(c) Local component check.** At any $p\in M$, choose a positively oriented
point-normal chart supplied by
[[thm-gr-point-normal-and-exponential-coordinate-charts]]. In that chart,
write $E_i(x):=-cF_{0i}(x)$ and
$B_i(x):=\frac12\epsilon_{ijk}F_{jk}(x)$, where $\epsilon_{123}=+1$ and
$\epsilon_{ijk}$ is alternating. These are local component abbreviations in
the chosen chart, not global observer fields. With
$\operatorname{div}E:=\partial_iE_i$,
$(\operatorname{curl}E)_k:=\epsilon_{kij}\partial_iE_j$, and similarly
for $B$, the pointwise component identities are

$$v^0=-\frac{1}{c}\operatorname{div}E,\qquad v^k=\frac{1}{c^2}\partial_tE_k-(\operatorname{curl}B)_k,$$

$$ (d\star_gF)_{123}=\frac{1}{c}\operatorname{div}E,\qquad (d\star_gF)_{0ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}\left(\frac{1}{c^2}\partial_tE_k-(\operatorname{curl}B)_k\right),$$

$$ (dF)_{123}=\operatorname{div}B,\qquad (dF)_{0ij}=\frac{\epsilon_{ijk}}{c}\left(\partial_tB_k+(\operatorname{curl}E)_k\right),$$

where $\partial_t:=c\,\partial_0$. The equations are pointwise identities
in normal coordinates; they do not assert that these component abbreviations
form global three-vector fields on curved spacetime.

On an open flat Minkowski domain with a fixed inertial Cartesian chart
$x^0=ct$, define $\rho:=j^0/c$, $J^i:=j^i$, and
$\epsilon_0:=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$. The same component formulas at every point give

$$\operatorname{div}E=\frac{\rho}{\epsilon_0},\qquad \operatorname{curl}B-\frac{1}{c^2}\partial_tE=\mu_0J,\qquad \operatorname{div}B=0,\qquad \partial_tB+\operatorname{curl}E=0.$$

These are a coordinate reduction of the stated tensor and form equations, not
claims that the smooth fields describe an experiment.

Let $(M,g,N,o)$ have the oriented, time-oriented Lorentzian structure and volume form of [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. On decomposable $k$-covectors define the induced exterior pairing by

$$\langle\alpha_1\wedge\cdots\wedge\alpha_k,\beta_1\wedge\cdots\wedge\beta_k\rangle_g:=\det\bigl(g^{-1}(\alpha_i,\beta_j)\bigr),$$

and extend it bilinearly. For $0\le k\le4$, its coordinate expression is the pointwise exterior metric on $k$-covectors

$$\langle\alpha,\beta\rangle_g:=\frac1{k!}\alpha_{a_1\cdots a_k}\beta^{a_1\cdots a_k},$$

where indices are raised by $g^{-1}$. There is a unique smooth bundle map $\star_g:\Omega^k(M)\to\Omega^{4-k}(M)$ characterized by

$$\alpha\wedge\star_g\beta=\langle\alpha,\beta\rangle_g\,\mathrm{vol}_g$$

at every point. In a positively oriented $g$-orthonormal coframe $(e^0,e^1,e^2,e^3)$, put $\epsilon_0=-1$ and $\epsilon_1=\epsilon_2=\epsilon_3=1$. For an increasing index set $I\subseteq\{0,1,2,3\}$, let $I^c$ be its increasing complement, let $s(I,I^c)$ be the sign of the permutation $(I,I^c)$ to $(0,1,2,3)$, and set $\epsilon_I:=\prod_{i\in I}\epsilon_i$. Let $M,a,q\in\mathbb R$ have units of metres. Write
$$\Sigma(r,\theta):=r^2+a^2\cos^2\theta,\quad \Delta(r):=r^2-2Mr+a^2+q^2,\quad R(r):=r^2+a^2,\quad B(\theta):=\sin^2\theta.$$

$\{(x^0,r,\theta,\phi):\Sigma>0,\ \Delta\ne0,\ 0<\theta<\pi\}$.
Coordinates $x^0,r$ have units of metres and $\theta,\phi$ are dimensionless.
On $U$ define
$$g=-\frac{\Delta}{\Sigma}(dx^0-aB\,d\phi)^2 +\frac{\Sigma}{\Delta}\,dr^2+\Sigma\,d\theta^2 +\frac{B}{\Sigma}(R\,d\phi-a\,dx^0)^2,\qquad \mathcal A=-\frac{qr}{\Sigma}(dx^0-aB\,d\phi),\quad\mathcal F:=d\mathcal A.$$
The metric is the exact real symmetric tensor given by this display; no value
on $\Delta=0$, the axes $\theta=0,\pi$, or $\Sigma=0$ is part of this
definition. The scalar $q$ is a geometric electric flux-length parameter; no
SI conversion is fixed in this Definition.

**Well-definedness on the stated patch.** In the coordinates
$(x^0,r,y,\phi)$ with $y=\cos\theta$ and $b=1-y^2$, the coordinate change is
a smooth diffeomorphism because $dy/d\theta=-\sin\theta\ne0$. The metric
matrix has
$$g_{00}=-\frac{\Delta-a^2b}{\Sigma},\quad g_{03}=-\frac{ab(R-\Delta)}{\Sigma},\quad g_{33}=\frac{b(R^2-a^2\Delta b)}{\Sigma},\quad g_{11}=\frac{\Sigma}{\Delta},\quad g_{22}=\frac{\Sigma}{b}.$$
The inverse has nonzero entries
$$g^{00}=-\frac{R^2-a^2\Delta b}{\Sigma\Delta},\quad g^{03}=-\frac{a(R-\Delta)}{\Sigma\Delta},\quad g^{33}=\frac{\Delta-a^2b}{\Sigma\Delta b},\quad g^{11}=\frac{\Delta}{\Sigma},\quad g^{22}=\frac{b}{\Sigma}.$$

hence is positive definite, while $g_{11}<0$ and $g_{22}>0$. Thus $g$ is

The potential is a smooth real one-form on $U$ because $\Sigma>0$, so $\mathcal F$

Applying it again pairs each second partial of a potential coefficient with its reversed-order partial and opposite wedge sign. Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and let $c>0$ be a fixed real constant.
All curves below take values in $M$; the physical reading of $c$, of a
worldline as the history of a clock or body, and of the parameter values as
times is not part of this definition and is adopted separately in the
postulates of the framework.

**(a) Regularity classes.** Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an interval with
nonempty interior ([[def-interval]]) and let $\gamma:I\to M$ be a map. A
**chart representative** of $\gamma$ is the map $x\circ\gamma$ for a smooth
chart $(U,x)$ of $M$ ([[def-smooth-manifold]]).

- For $k\in\mathbb N_0\cup\{\infty\}$ and an interior point $t_0\in I$, the map
  $\gamma$ is **$C^k$ at $t_0$** when there is a chart representative
  $x\circ\gamma$ defined near $t_0$ that is $C^k$ there in the componentwise
  Euclidean sense. This condition is independent of the chart: on the overlap
  of two chart representatives the transition map is smooth and the chain rule
  applies ([[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]],
  [[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]]). If $t_0\in I$ is an
  included endpoint of $I$, the coordinate representative and its derivatives through order $k$
  are continuous up to $t_0$ on the relative interval
  $I\cap(t_0-\delta,t_0+\delta)$ for some $\delta>0$, with derivatives at
  $t_0$ taken one-sided. For $k=\infty$ this holds at every finite order.
  Merely possessing a one-sided secant tangent, as defined next, does not
  by itself make a curve $C^1$ at the endpoint. The map $\gamma$ is **$C^k$ on $I$** when it is $C^k$ at
  every point of $I$.

- Let $b\in\mathbb R$ and $\varepsilon>0$. A curve
  $\gamma:(b-\varepsilon,b]\to M$ has **left tangent** $v\in T_{\gamma(b)}M$
  at $b$ when for one — equivalently every — chart $(U,x)$ around
  $\gamma(b)$, writing $v=\sum_{a=0}^{3}v^a\partial_a|_{\gamma(b)}$
  ([[thm-coordinate-derivations-form-a-basis-of-the-tangent-space]]), the
  difference quotients satisfy
  $\bigl(x^a(\gamma(t))-x^a(\gamma(b))\bigr)/(t-b)\to v^a$ as $t\uparrow b$ for
  $a=0,1,2,3$. A **right tangent** at the left end of a curve is defined
  analogously with $t\downarrow b$. Chart independence is the one-sided
  chain-rule computation for the smooth transition maps
  ([[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]]).

- A curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ with $a<b$ is **piecewise $C^1$** when there is a
  finite partition $a=s_0<s_1<\cdots<s_m=b$ such that for every $i$ the
  restriction of $\gamma$ to $[s_{i-1},s_i]$ is $C^1$ up to its included
  endpoints in the one-sided sense above: in every endpoint chart its
  component derivatives on the open piece have continuous one-sided limits,
  agreeing with its endpoint derivatives. Equivalently each piece has a
  $C^1$ extension to its closed parameter piece. In particular its right
  tangent at $s_{i-1}$ and left tangent at $s_i$ exist. Such a
  partition is called **admissible** for $\gamma$. The piece extensions give continuity at the
  corners; no agreement of the
  two one-sided tangents at a corner is required.

**(b) Velocity.** If $\gamma$ is $C^1$ at an interior point $t$, its
**velocity** $\gamma'(t)\in T_{\gamma(t)}M$ is the derivation
$[f]\mapsto(f\circ\gamma)'(t)$ on smooth germs at $\gamma(t)$, extending
[[def-velocity-derivation-of-a-smooth-curve]] from smooth to $C^1$ curves.
Equal germ representatives agree along the curve near $t$, and the
one-variable product rule proves the derivation identity. In a chart around
$\gamma(t)$ the velocity has the component
expression

$$\gamma'(t)=\sum_{a=0}^{3}\frac{d}{dt}\bigl(x^a\circ\gamma\bigr)(t)\,\partial_a|_{\gamma(t)},$$

the coordinate expression of the derivation
([[thm-coordinate-derivations-form-a-basis-of-the-tangent-space]]). At an
included endpoint of the domain, $\gamma'$ means the corresponding one-sided
tangent of clause (a).

**(c) Timelike worldlines.** For $k\in\{1,2,3,\ldots\}\cup\{\infty\}$,
a **$C^k$ future timelike worldline** is a $C^k$
curve $\gamma:I\to M$ whose velocity $\gamma'(t)$ is future timelike at every
$t\in I$, in the sense of [[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]]
and [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]: $g_{\gamma(t)}(\gamma'(t),\gamma'(t))<0$
and $g_{\gamma(t)}(\gamma'(t),N_{\gamma(t)})<0$. A **piecewise-$C^1$ future
timelike worldline** is a piecewise-$C^1$ curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ whose
velocity at every point of each open piece and whose one-sided tangents at the
two ends of each piece are future timelike; the definition is applied to a map
on an arbitrary interval $I$ with nonempty interior by requiring it on every
compact subinterval of $I$. A future timelike velocity is in particular
nonzero, so every future timelike worldline is regular.

**(d) Proper time and length.** Let $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ be a piecewise-$C^1$
future timelike worldline and let $a=s_0<s_1<\cdots<s_m=b$ be an admissible
partition. On each open piece $(s_{i-1},s_i)$ the function

$$h_i(s):=\sqrt{-g_{\gamma(s)}\bigl(\gamma'(s),\gamma'(s)\bigr)}$$

is continuous and strictly positive: it is a finite sum of products of
continuous real functions in any chart around a point of the piece, as
$g_{ab}\circ\gamma$ and the components of $\gamma'$ are continuous
([[thm-componentwise-limits-and-continuity]],
[[thm-algebra-of-continuous-functions]], [[def-continuity-real]]), and the
square root is continuous on $(0,\infty)$ ([[def-rational-power]],
[[thm-real-power-continuity-and-derivatives]]). The continuous one-sided limits of the component derivatives, required
by the $C^1$ extension of each piece, and continuity of $g$ imply that
$h_i$ tends to the norm of the corresponding endpoint tangent. The future
timelike hypothesis on those tangents makes these limits strictly positive, and $h_i$ extends to a continuous function on
$[s_{i-1},s_i]$; hence it is Darboux integrable there
([[def-darboux-integral]], [[thm-continuous-implies-integrable]]). The
**proper-time increment** of $\gamma$ over $[a,b]$ is

$$\tau(b)-\tau(a):=\frac{1}{c}\sum_{i=1}^{m}\int_{s_{i-1}}^{s_i}h_i(s)\,ds,$$

and the **Lorentzian length** of $\gamma$ over $[a,b]$ is
$L_g(\gamma):=c\,(\tau(b)-\tau(a))$. For a base point $s_0\in I$ the
**proper-time function** $\tau:I\to\mathbb R$ of a future timelike worldline is
the function with $\tau(s_0)=0$ and $\tau(s)$ equal to the increment
from $s_0$ to $s$ when $s>s_0$, and minus the increment from $s$ to $s_0$
when $s<s_0$. That the increment is independent of the admissible
partition, so that $\tau$ is well defined, and that it is invariant under
increasing $C^1$ reparametrization with strictly positive derivative
(including one-sided endpoint derivatives), comparing the increment over the
actual image interval, are proved in
[[lem-gr-proper-time-reparametrization-and-four-velocity]]; the display is the
value for any admissible partition.

**(e) Four-velocity.** Let $\gamma$ be a piecewise-$C^1$ future timelike
worldline and let $t$ be a parameter value at which $\gamma$ is differentiable
(interior point of a piece, or an included endpoint with its one-sided
tangent). The **four-velocity** of $\gamma$ at $t$ is

$$U(t):=\frac{c\,\gamma'(t)}{\sqrt{-g_{\gamma(t)}\bigl(\gamma'(t),\gamma'(t)\bigr)}}\in T_{\gamma(t)}M .$$

By construction $g_{\gamma(t)}(U(t),U(t))=-c^2$, and
$\gamma'(t)=\bigl(\sqrt{-g(\gamma',\gamma')}/c\bigr)U(t)$ with a strictly
positive scalar factor. If $U$ is written as the derivative of $\gamma$ with
respect to proper time, $U=d\gamma/d\tau$, this is a statement proved in
[[lem-gr-proper-time-reparametrization-and-four-velocity]], not part of the
present definition.

**(f) Scope.** Proper time, length and four-velocity are defined only for
future timelike worldlines. A null or spacelike curve receives no proper time
and no four-velocity from this definition, and no limiting or distributional
extension of the square-root integrand to such curves is asserted. The
parametrization of a worldline is part of the data and is arbitrary in this
definition: no affine parameter, no geodesic equation, no completeness or
extendability of the domain, and no measurement or clock reading is assumed.
Null and spacelike regularity classes are not defined here beyond the general
$C^k$ and piecewise-$C^1$ notions of clause (a), which make no causal
requirement.
